Theorem(4.14), printed p.423 (PDF p.19), original formula visually checked
verification_scope: For a parallelism on a (4k-1)-manifold the original real Adams invariant is epsilon(k) times the reduced Dirac eta invariant minus its connection transgression. The exact coefficient is epsilon(k)=1/2 for k odd. On the flat Lie-framed T3, k=1, the connection term is zero, paired Fourier eigenvalues give eta=0, and periodic spinors have complex dimension2. Hence the real invariant is (1/2)(2/2)=1/2 modZ. The complex invariant alone would be0 and is not substituted for the real one.
limits: The exact formula and its printed derivation were read; no full independent verification of the APS boundary index theorem is asserted.

verification_scope: Proposition8.3.5 makes E1^(p,q)=H^q(X_p,Z)⇒H^(p+q)(X_bullet,Z) a spectral sequence of mixed Hodge structures for a separated simplicial scheme. At C3=0 the finite 2Z3 toroidal cover has smooth projective toric strata and algebraic face maps. Add the degenerate simplices to the finite normalization semisimplicial scheme; its normalized alternating complex is unchanged. Each H^q(stratum,Q) is pure of weightq, so E2^(p,q) is pure of weightq. For r>=2 the differential changes q to q-r+1 and is therefore zero. Finite deck invariants are exact overQ. The explicitly computed integral E2 groups are free, so rational vanishing implies integral vanishing inductively, and extensions of free abelian groups remain free.
limits: This is the Hodge III source for the normalization weight argument; the separately opened Deligne1970 regular-connections book does not supply this scope. Integral invariant-cycle surjectivity is not inferred from mixed-Hodge degeneration: it uses the separately printed explicit line-bundle descent and saturated lattice calculation.
